hero.headline: Heritage Plantation residents seek help as more rain threatens flooded homes
hero.teaser: Residents of the mobile home park near Vero Beach say repeated flooding has sent water into homes, damaged vehicles and complicated emergency access. Indian River County has extended its state of emergency through Nov. 30.
hero.body:
Residents of Heritage Plantation near Vero Beach are pleading for help as more heavy rain threatens the mobile home park after repeated flooding this month. Residents described water entering a home, costly vehicle damage and difficulty getting emergency responders to a neighbor in need of medical assistance.

 Joe Waters recorded a car driving through floodwaters that nearly covered its headlights outside his mobile home Saturday evening. He said the wake from passing vehicles knocked over bricks protecting his home's undercarriage. “The water came up probably about thigh high,” Waters said. “Came up into the driveway, went into the house.” Waters and his wife were able to clean their home, but he said his car remained in the shop with $4,600 worth of damage while he awaited insurance approval.

 Dawn Carboni, the HOA president, said flooding also complicated an EMS response. Emergency responders could not reach one man's home and had to park on 82nd Avenue, she said. A large fire truck then had to reach the home. Carboni said she wants to speak for her neighbors, especially those who cannot speak up for themselves. “They just want to feel safe in their homes,” she said.

 With more heavy rain in the forecast, Carboni said residents fear being unable to leave their homes. “People are afraid. It's horrible living in fear when you don't know if it's going to rain and you're going to be able to leave your home the next day.” She urged help for the community: “We need help, and we're asking for help,” Carboni said.

 Indian River County emergency managers said the county is operating at a Level 2 emergency, with the Emergency Operations Center partially activated. The county has extended its state of emergency through Nov. 30.
